The call Trace
Calderwick can service its debt today, but every measure of strain moved the wrong way in FY2026, and an EBITDA fall of 23.3% would reach its leverage limit.

Net leverage is 4.6x against a limit of 6.0x and interest cover is 2.7x against a floor of 2.0x. Debt grew faster than earnings, so room to both limits is smaller than a year ago. The 2028 term loan B of 640 is the repayment to watch.

Key findings
  1. 1Adjusted EBITDA rose 2.7% to 378, but debt rose faster, so net leverage edged up to 4.6x from 4.5x.Trace
  2. 2Interest cover slipped to 2.7x from 2.9x as cash interest rose 11.1% to 140.Trace
  3. 3Room to both covenant levels is smaller: leverage headroom is 23.3% (was 25.0%) and cover headroom 25.9% (was 31.5%).Trace
  4. 4790 of the 1,890 debt falls due by the end of 2028, and the 640 term loan B is the largest repayment.Trace
  5. 5A severe downside (EBITDA down 24%) breaches the leverage limit; a combined case (down 30%) breaches both.Trace
Contrary evidence
Revenue grew 5.0% and EBITDA 2.7%, so the weaker ratios come from more debt and more interest, not from weaker trading.
What would change the view
Resolved favourablyThe term loan B is refinanced early at or below its current cost and net leverage falls under 4.5x.
Resolved adverselyEBITDA falls by about a quarter before 2028, or the revolver is not extended past 2027.

Bottom line by module

✓Source readiness Every module that ran found the files it needed.

✓Financial foundation Revenue grew 5.0% to 1,932 and EBITDA 2.7% to 378; net debt rose to 1,739.

✓Earnings changes Margin slipped to 19.6% from 20.0% as costs grew faster than sales.

⊘Peer benchmark Not assessable: no peer data was supplied.

✓Earnings quality Reported EBITDA is backed by cash flow; the adjustments are small and recur each year.

✓Business & governance Packaging for food makers; one sponsor controls the board.

✓Research questions The open questions for management are the revolver's draw dates and the plan for the 2028 term loan B.

✓Fundamental credit Sound cash generation, but thinner room to the limits than a year ago.

✓Downside The first break is a 23.3% EBITDA fall, at the leverage limit.

!Liquidity Limited: committed resources are 351; the revolver's draw dates are not stated.

✓Rates, FX & hedging Most of the term loan B's floating-rate interest is hedged; there is no foreign-exchange exposure of note.

✓Forward credit model Net leverage peaks at 4.8x in FY2027 in the base case.

!Security selection Limited: no market quotes, so no value per security.

✓Refinancing & LME 790 falls due by the end of 2028; the 640 term loan B is the largest.

✓Legal & covenants Both tests pass today, with 23.3% and 25.9% headroom.

✓Evidence validation Usable by the committee with two medium issues open.

✓Committee decision Hold the credit view until the 2028 term loan B is addressed.
